problem: Zero-shot MLLM navigators expose history either through dense semantic maps (storage grows with mapped area, built separately from decisions) or raw visual histories (context grows with trajectory, landmarks buried, dead ends not marked). In neither case does the MLLM decide what to retain.
motivation: Long-horizon zero-shot VLN needs to know where the robot has been, how the instruction has progressed and which branches failed, without ever-growing context. The paper adapts generative-agent memory principles to spatial navigation, so the same model call that picks the action also writes memory.
key_idea: Let the System-2 MLLM write structured semantic, progress and failure notes into a depth-grounded place-object world graph in the same call that selects the action, and retrieve a subgoal-conditioned graph slice (relevance/recency/salience plus one-hop topology) instead of raw image history.
insight: Larger raw-history windows raise tokens monotonically but do not improve SR/SPL (K=3 to full: API tokens +98.7%, SR -4.7, SPL -6.6), so selective retrieval matters more than more context. Ablations show all parts matter: removing the world graph costs 9.3 SR at K=1, and removing reflection memory drops SPL by 11.2 (48.1 to 36.9), so failure notes mainly improve path efficiency.
method: Dual-process architecture: System 2 (Gemini-3.1-Pro) is called once per waypoint and outputs a JSON decision (direction, backtrack or stop) with progress analysis; System 1 (Qwen3.6-35B) predicts a bounding box in the chosen view and a deterministic controller back-projects it with depth and odometry and executes it via fast-marching planning.

Sparse grounded world graph: typed place-object graph with place-place and place-object edges; places come from incremental single-link clustering and objects from Grounding DINO + SAM detections projected through depth. Persistent state grows with discovered places, not with area.

Decision-coupled memory writes: the same System-2 call outputs place semantics, observed objects, instruction-progress updates and rationale; these update the progress record L and the graph G with no extra LLM calls.

Four memory views: working memory (verbatim frames of the last K waypoints, K=1), episodic (temporal visitation, recency), semantic (place-object content, relevance), reflection (failure notes resurfacing when a place is retrieved).

Subgoal-conditioned retrieval: the score s = 1.0*relevance (bge-large cosine to the current subgoal) + 0.3*recency (0.85^dt) + 0.3*salience; top K_s=3 seeds, one-hop expansion plus the current-place neighborhood, at most K_p=5 places serialized into the context.

Grounded failure memory for backtracking: on backtrack, the abandoned suffix is mapped to place states and the rationale is stored as advisory place-level failure evidence, without changing scores or blocking places.

setting.backbone: Gemini-3.1-Pro (System 2 planner, frozen) + Qwen3.6-35B (System 1 grounding, frozen) + Grounding DINO/SAM + bge-large-en-v1.5 retrieval encoder
setting.action_space: high-level direction/backtrack/stop chosen by MLLM, converted to pixel targets and then low-level motion via fast-marching local planning
setting.privileged: none (uses odometry pose and depth as standard)

numbers.extra: K=1 working window; 17.9k S2 tokens/decision, 244.9k API tokens/episode

numbers_note: Split for HM3D-v2 ObjectNav is not stated explicitly beyond 'val-unseen subsets'. All evaluations use 100-episode subsets, so they are not directly comparable to full-split numbers.
results: Zero-shot HAM-VLN reaches 61.0 SR / 48.1 SPL on R2R-CE, 52.7 SR on RxR-CE and 79.7 SR / 43.2 SPL on HM3D-v2 ObjectNav. It beats the best training-free baselines by 22.7 SR on R2R-CE (vs Three-Step Nav) and 18.9 SR on RxR-CE (vs GC-VLN), and beats ApexNav (76.2 SR) on ObjectNav. It also beats full raw history with 67% fewer API tokens per episode, but the strongest trained VLN systems (e.g. OmniNav 69.5 SR) remain higher.
limitations: Evaluated only on 100-episode subsets with a very strong proprietary MLLM (Gemini-3.1-Pro), so cost, latency and comparability to full-split results are uncertain; no real-robot tests.
Still below the best supervised VLN methods in SR/SPL, and SPL is well below SR (frequent backtracking: 1.75 per episode).
Relies on hand-set retrieval weights and budgets and on external detectors (Grounding DINO/SAM); the memory design is fixed rather than learned.
